shifts.summary: The exam was overall easy to moderate with most candidates attempting 77 to 89 questions well. Reasoning was generally easy, while quantitative aptitude leaned moderate. General awareness was easy for many, and English was easy overall. Time management and the new sectional timer were common concerns.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported many statement‑based and matrix questions, with no clock or mirror types. Reasoning was generally easy, some found it very easy.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK mix included current affairs and static topics, candidates found it easy overall.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was moderate overall, with many circle and trigonometry questions; time management was noted as a concern.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was easy for most candidates, with grammar and active‑passive questions common; passages were moderate in length.

asked.q: Tagore wrote a national song for Bangladesh

observations: Candidates noted time management was a challenge, especially in math and reasoning sections.
The paper pattern remained similar to previous years with no major changes.
A 15‑minute sectional timer caused difficulty for many candidates.
Overall attempts were high, with many reporting 85‑89 well‑attempted questions.
disagreements: Overall difficulty was split between Easy to Moderate (3 reports) and Moderate (3 reports).
Quant difficulty was reported as Easy by three sources and Moderate by six sources.

intro: The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam held on 7 October 2026 has been analysed based on the reports from the three shifts. Unofficial figures suggest that the overall difficulty ranged from easy to moderate, with good attempt rates varying between 75 and 89 questions across shifts. SSC typically normalises scores across shifts to ensure fairness. The analysis for shift 3 is still incomplete and will be added once the full data is available.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: According to the reported data, the exam was generally classified as easy to moderate, although some candidates noted sections that felt harder, especially in quantitative aptitude.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt on average in the 7 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: The unofficial attempt ranges were 77–89 for shift 1, 79–84.2 for shift 2, and 75–86 for shift 3, indicating most candidates answered between three‑quarters and four‑fifths of the paper.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as easiest and hardest on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was generally reported as the easiest section, while quantitative aptitude showed mixed difficulty, ranging from easy to hard, and English was noted as difficult in shift 3 due to lengthy passages.

faqs.q: Did candidates face any time‑management issues on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, time management and the new sectional timer were cited as common concerns, particularly in shift 1 where long graphs in reasoning and lengthy passages in English affected pacing.

faqs.q: Will the analysis for shift 3 of the 7 October 2026 exam be updated?
faqs.a: The analysis for shift 3 is currently partial; a complete summary will be added after the full data for that shift is released.
